To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a SPAK kinase isoform switch along the nephron modulates blood pressure.

a kidney-specific splice variant of SPAK inhibits NCC and NKCCC phosphorylation and that the differential expression of the two isoforms along the distal convoluded tubule and thick ascending limb modulates sodium avidness along the distal renal tubule and contributes to the control of blood pressure.

a kidney-specific isoform of the kinase SPAK inhibits the phosphorylation of NKCC2 and NCD by full-length SPAk, and that the differential expression of these two isoforms along the nephron is critical for blood pressure regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of salt transporters in the kidney, which is important for understanding the pathogenesis of high blood pressure.
a mechanism for the differential modulation of NKCC2 and NCD in the distal nephrons.
the role of SPAK and OSRI in the control of renal salt transport and hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPAK isoform switches modulate salt transport along the distal tubule and thereby blood pressure.
a SPAK kinase switch modulates renal sodium transport, and blood pressure, by regulating the phosphorylation of Ncc and Nkcc2.
the SPAK isoform switches are important for the regulation of salt homeostasis in the distal tubule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPAK isoform expression is differentially regulated and this isoform switch is a mechanism to regulate salt balance and blood pressure.
SPAK isoform switches in kidney regulate renal sodium handling in health and disease.
the kidney-specific isoform of SPAK inhibits the activity of the full-length SPAK and that this inhibition is important to maintain the balance between salt retention and excretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the kidney has the ability to regulate its salt transport machinery by altering the expression of SPAK isoforms, and that SPAK isoform switching is a mechanism that can be exploited to treat salt-sensitive hypertension.

the SPAK kinase domain is not required for regulation of renal salt transport and that the kidney-specific isoform of SPAK may serve as a molecular switch that regulates salt transport along the distal renal tubule in response to changes in extracellular volume.
SPAK isoform switching modulates salt transport and blood pressure.
